hero.title: File:RAF Brawdy aerial view 1944.jpg
hero.credit: This photograph HU 92993 comes from the collections of the Imperial War Museums.
hero.description: Vertical aerial view of RAF Brawdy, Pembrokeshire (UK). Although it was used as a satellite airfield by the nearby St David's at this time, Brawdy did not officially open until February 1944 when No. 517 Squadron RAF moved there to fly meteorological sorties over the Atlantic Ocean and the Western approaches.

gallery.title: File:Hawk XX315 at Manston 1986 (52095781434).jpg
gallery.description: Royal Air Force (RAF) BAe Hawk T.1 XX315 from No. 1 Tactical Weapons Unit (1TWU) at RAF Brawdy.  The unit moved to RAF Valley when Brawdy closed in 1992, and XX315 joined No. 4 Flying Training School (4FTS) there.  It was loaned to the Royal Navy (RN) FRADU at RNAS Yeovilton in 1995, and returned to RAF 4FTS at Valley in 2001.  It eventually went into store at RAF Shawbury in 2016.  Photo: Dick Gilbert, RAF Manston 70th Anniversary Open Day, 31 May 1986.
